llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Kia Access MCP setup that can read vehicle data and run confirm-gated vehicle commands, with notable but purpose-aligned credential and session-token handling risks.

dimensions.detail: Access to vehicle location and real-world vehicle commands is high impact, but it is coherent with the skill purpose and includes read/write mode separation plus user confirmation for commands.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup runs an external npm MCP package through npx and asks the user to place Kia credentials in MCP environment configuration; this is disclosed and common for MCP setup, but users should treat that config as sensitive.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Command behavior is scoped by KIA_WRITE_MODE, requires confirm, previews dry runs when confirm is absent, and includes cautions for stale reads, unlock risk, failed logins, and secret handling.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill documents a persistent remember-me token that can silently refresh sessions and an exported refresh token that bypasses MFA; it also documents kia_forget_session and warns not to expose the token.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's vehicle status, location, charging, climate, lock, and unlock capabilities match its stated Kia Access purpose and are explicitly documented as using the user's own account.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving this MCP server access to your Kia account and vehicle controls. Use KIA_WRITE_MODE=none unless you need commands, protect any .mcp.json or ~/.claude/mcp.json containing Kia credentials, and avoid exporting or sharing the refresh token except for a deployment you control.
llm.findings:
[AS2] expected: The plaintext Kia username/password configuration and refresh-token handling are real sensitive-data considerations, but they are disclosed and directly support authentication for the intended Kia Access MCP workflow.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger phrase includes a broad Kia-vehicle catch-all, but it remains domain-scoped to Kia vehicle read or command requests and the risky commands are further gated by write mode and confirm.
